summary: R2 substantively closes the four R1 blockers: §3.3 now confines Prop. 19.2 to fixed-channel use, β.4 is rewritten as an open structural comparison with an explicit Σ-map requirement and no proof sketch, the old "closes β.Gx" upgrade language and combined-chain claim are removed, and §9 now cleanly separates PDF verification from novel-proof work. I did not find a reappearance of the β.5 critical misuse or any new combined-chain overclaim. The remaining blocker is narrower but still disqualifying under your stated acceptance rule: the draft still presents some paraphrased or inferred literature support as if it were literal verified citation content.

issues.description: The document still overstates citation fidelity. Several cited statements are phrased as verified/literal support even though they are paraphrases or inferences rather than exact source text: the Sec. 20.1 product-state support at line 57, the Prop. 19.2 bullet framed as "literal content" at lines 76-79, and the Ch. 20 adaptive-LOCC characterization at line 146. Because your Round 2 acceptance criteria require citations to remain literal and non-paraphrastic, this is a new evidentiary over-claim even though the underlying structural claims are now marked open.
issues.suggestion: Where support must be literal, quote only exact source wording/equations and keep any interpretation outside the quotation. Otherwise relabel these items explicitly as paraphrased summaries or inferences, and remove the "no paraphrase / literal content" framing from §3.3 and any similar bullets.

round_recommendation: Replace paraphrased VERIFIED bullets with exact quoted source text or mark them as summaries/inferences, then rerun the review. All structural R1 issues otherwise appear closed.
